title: Mini-QBR decision grid and ops briefing for runtime bets
creator: Asha Rao
description: Purpose: produce a concise, operational Mini-QBR packet (one A4 + 1 decision grid) for exec readout that summarizes proposed investments across runtime capabilities (batching, KV caching, kernel selection) and the recommended funding/engine time for the next quarter. Scope: evaluate three investment lanes (Performance, Cost, Reliability) using a 2x2 effort vs impact decision grid and call out clear tradeoffs and roll-out gating criteria. Outcome: a validated ask (M/ask) to present at the weekly exec readout and a prioritized 6-week runbook for the engineering squad. Rationale: full QBR decks have been too long; this micro-format aims to speed decisions while keeping execs informed and enabling ops handoffs. Deliverables: 1) one-page decision grid, 2) 6-week tactical runbook with owners, 3) risk & rollback lanes, 4) quick dashboard links for supporting metrics.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Asha Rao (PM): Drafted the decision grid and initial scoring for lanes. Attached baseline metrics: 95th latency, token-cost per request, KV hit-rate. Asked Eng for estimate sanity check.

2026-02-27 - Mateo Alvarez (ENG Lead): Reviewed lane definitions. Suggest splitting Performance into 'cold-start latency' and 'steady-state latency' because kernel selection impacts them differently. Estimate +2 points on complexity for kernel work.
2026-03-01 - Priya Shah (Design): Raised UX concern for internal console surface: rollouts and canary signals need clearer visualization; proposed a compact time-series sparkline per route.
2026-03-03 - Liam Chen (Assignee, PM): Incorporated feedback, updated effort estimates and created the tactical runbook. Punted the kernel split to 'follow on' with rationale documented.

2026-03-05 - SRE Team (comment): Noted operational dependency on autoscaler tuning (ENG-45122) and possible short-term capacity risk if we prioritize aggressive batching changes during peak hours. Recommend a canary policy and surge fallback.

2026-03-09 - Asha Rao (PM): Packet pushed to exec folder and shared in #exec-readout for asynchronous review. Added two ask lanes: 1) reallocate 0.5 FTE from infra to runtime for 6 weeks; 2) authorize $120k experimental pool for dedicated capacity testing.
2026-03-10 - Liam Chen (Assignee): Updated runbook with owners, added dashboard links and GitHub PR references. Ready for review by Head of Product on 2026-03-11.
decisions: Decision 1: Prioritize Cost lane (intelligent batching + quantization pilot) as the top bet for Q2 due to highest estimated ROI and <8 week engineering cadence.
Decision 2: Defer kernel-heavy steady-state latency work to follow-on runway; perform small experiment for kernel selection heuristics only as a spike in Week 2.
Decision 3: Approve temporary 0.5 FTE shift for 6 weeks and a $120k dedicated capacity pool for controlled A/B testing with two enterprise customers (opt-in).
Decision 4: Require SLO-preserving canary policy and surge fallback prior to any production batching parameter changes.
tradeoffs: Performance vs Cost: Aggressive batching reduces unit cost but increases 95th latency for low-concurrency short requests; recommended limited-window rollouts and route exclusions.
Speed of rollout vs Observability: Faster experiments increase risk; mitigated by short canaries, feature flags, and enhanced trace sampling for affected routes.
Engineering focus vs Platform stability: Kernel optimizations have high upside but long lead time; cost-focused work delivers measurable savings faster.

Week 1: Create feature flag + rollout plan and automated smoke tests (Owner: Liam Chen, due 2026-03-19)

notes: Designed to be read in under 5 minutes by execs. The one-pager distills OKR alignment: ties to 'Reduce inference cost per 1M tokens' (OKR-2026-Q2) and 'Maintain 95th latency SLOs'. This format reduces slide churn and focuses discussion on binary funding decisions.
